text:
andrea: Ran a short nsys + heap-profiling pass on the kernel-swap rollout. Observed a ~2.4GB workspace growth over 30s on a steady 8k token stream. attaching flame snippet below (trimmed).

andrea: Flame top looks like: kernel_select -> continuous_batcher -> kv_insert -> allocate_workspace. Strange that allocate_workspace keeps increasing after decode finishes. :thinking:

raj: hmm, could be kernel selection switching to a different codepath that allocs larger scratch buffers per-request. did you correlate with model variant?

andrea: yes — it only appears on the 2nd-gen conv-attn kernel (fallback path when seq>1024). single-gpu test with same model version.

morgan: also saw some spikes in production traces yesterday. those requests had high batched_size variance. when we forced batching window to 8ms the spikes reduced. might be batching heuristic interacting with workspace sizing.

lee: pasted nsys excerpt:
```
# nsys: GPU allocations (top)
alloc_id  size   stack
0x7f1e   512MB  allocator::allocate_workspace()
0x7f2a   256MB  kernel::conv_attn::temp_buf()
0x7f3b   128MB  kv_cache::prefetch_slot()
```

lee: also saw repeated small frees that don't reclaim due to fragmentation, so free list stays fragmented.

andrea: ok fragmentation + larger per-kernel scratch = effective leak. maybe our slab allocator's free coalescing didn't run because of lock contention.

raj: quick thought: add a soft-reserve threshold for the conv-attn kernel path so it refuses to switch if free contiguous chunk < X. fallback to a decode-only kernel (higher latency) rather than allocating a huge workspace.

morgan: tradeoff: that avoids OOM but increases tail latency. we should measure where the client SLO breakpoint is. i can run A/B with soft-reserve=1.2GB vs 2.0GB.

taylor: another lever: buffer-reuse pool for temp kernel buffers. instead of alloc/free per-infer, keep a small cache keyed by (device, kernel_id, size_bucket). reuse reduces churn and fragmentation. cheap to implement in allocator layer.

andrea: +1 for reuse pool. can you sketch config knobs?

taylor: config snippet idea: 
```
allocator:
  reuse_pool:
    enabled: true
    max_per_bucket: 8
    size_buckets: [64MB,128MB,256MB,512MB]
  soft_reserve_bytes: 1200000000
  coalesce_window_ms: 50
```

lee: note: coalesce_window_ms trades latency for better compaction. if we wait a short time we can merge freed fragments into larger chunks. but this requires GC work on the allocator thread. watch CPU usage.

morgan: i can run microbench with continuous batching + seq lengths 512/1536 and compare three configs: baseline, reuse_pool enabled, soft_reserve-only. will post numbers.

andrea: perf regression angle — this only regressed after the kernel-swap patch. we should try forcing the old kernel codepath for a canary group and compare memory churn metrics.

raj: i'll open a short-lived feature flag to gate kernel-swap per-pod. label: kernel_swap_gate.

sre-bot: created INC-4789 for "kernel-swap memory churn / allocator fragmentation" and linked to #oncall.incident.

andrea: action items: (1) morgan run microbench and post results (2) taylor prototype reuse pool + config (3) raj enable kernel_swap_gate for canary (4) lee run nsys on canary vs prod kernels. aim to sync in 24h.

morgan: starting bench now, ETA ~4h. will output a CSV and a short summary. :rocket:

andrea: thanks — looks like we have both a policy and allocator-level fixes to try. if reuse_pool + soft_reserve removes spike without latency regression we can roll to canary next week.
